description:
A developer is organizing their project files under /home/user/project. Inside this directory, there is a file called file_list.txt which lists the paths of source code files (one per line, may include directories, filenames, extensions). The file contains mixed entries: some lines include full paths (like src/main.c), some just filenames (README.md), and some lines are comments starting with #. The developer needs your help performing these text processing steps: 1. Remove all lines that start with # (treated as comments) from /home/user/project/file_list.txt. 2. For each remaining line, extract only the base filename (i.e., remove the directory path, just keep the filename and extension, not including any parent directories). 3. Filter out all files whose extensions are .md or .txt (case-insensitive). 4. Alphabetically sort the resulting filenames and remove any duplicate entries. 5. Output this list to /home/user/project/organized_files.txt in this format:
  • Each filename occupies a separate line, in alphabetical order.
  • No empty lines or trailing whitespace.
6. Create a log file, /home/user/project/organization_log.txt, documenting:
  • a timestamp (in UTC, ISO 8601 format, e.g. 2024-06-17T15:45:22Z),
  • the number of filenames processed (after removing comments and extracting basenames),
  • the number of files excluded due to .md or .txt extension,
  • the number of unique files written to organized_files.txt.
Format the log as: 
[Timestamp] Processed: N, Excluded: M, Written: K
where N is processed (after comments removed, base extracted), M is excluded, K is unique names written. Provide no extra lines, only the single-line log entry. Your solution should use awk and sed for all text extraction and filtering. Place your output files only in /home/user/project.
